record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Ordered and Orderable Groups
record.original_question: What is the cardinality of the set of all subvarieties of R without covers (in R)?

evidence.quote: 1.32∗ . What is the cardinality of the set of all subvarieties of R without covers (in R)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{L}$ denote the variety of lattice-ordered groups (i.e., groups equipped with a lattice order compatible with the group operation, viewed as algebras in the signature $(\cdot,{}^{-1},e,\vee,\wedge)$), and let $\mathcal{R}\subseteq\mathcal{L}$ denote the variety of representable lattice-ordered groups, namely those lattice-ordered groups that are subdirect products of totally ordered groups. The collection of all subvarieties of $\mathcal{R}$ forms a complete lattice $\mathrm{Lat}(\mathcal{R})$ under inclusion. For a subvariety $\mathcal{V}\in\mathrm{Lat}(\mathcal{R})$, a cover of $\mathcal{V}$ in $\mathcal{R}$ is a subvariety $\mathcal{W}\in\mathrm{Lat}(\mathcal{R})$ such that $\mathcal{V}\subsetneq\mathcal{W}$ and there is no subvariety $\mathcal{U}\in\mathrm{Lat}(\mathcal{R})$ with $\mathcal{V}\subsetneq\mathcal{U}\subsetneq\mathcal{W}$. Determine the cardinality of the set
$$\{\mathcal{V}\in\mathrm{Lat}(\mathcal{R}) : \mathcal{V}\text{ has no cover in }\mathcal{R}\}.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears to remain open. The standard reference compilation of unsolved problems in ordered and orderable groups lists this question with an asterisk indicating it is unsolved, and current literature on the lattice of subvarieties of representable ℓ-groups discusses only partial results (e.g., known examples of subvarieties without covers and structural results by Medvedev and others), without giving a precise cardinality.
